title: Transport contract and loopback transport

parent.objective: Bring up a host-side bridge for the fictional SYNTH-SENSOR-1 so that every component is verified independently and no hardware behavior is claimed before it is observed.

goal: Define the Transport protocol and a loopback implementation that preserves order and times out instead of blocking.
non_goals: Communicate with, or claim behavior of, any physical device.

prohibited: Edit codec, device, adapter or telemetry modules.

inputs.name: Transport contract
inputs.description: send(bytes) and receive(timeout_s) -> bytes; receive raises TransportTimeout when nothing is available.

interface.name: synth_bridge.transport
interface.description: Byte-frame transport contract; loopback echoes sent frames in order.

assumptions: Loopback behavior is a simulation of an ordered link, not evidence of one.

sources.authority: Synthetic specification invented for this example; not a manufacturer document.

sources.reference: examples/software-hardware/sample — the synthetic bridge package and its tests
sources.authority: Reference implementation for this example only; establishes no real device behavior.

acceptance_criteria.description: Frames are received in the order they were sent, as copies.
An empty receive raises TransportTimeout; a negative timeout is refused.

architecture_boundaries: Do not change the Transport contract signatures.
No physical port access outside the adapter packet.

hardware_assumptions.assumption: A physical serial link delivers whole frames in order without duplication within the read timeout.
